sections.heading: Bottom-up estimates
sections.detail: committed first — timestamp above, before any market number
sections.markdown:
**Sources (primary, accessed 2026-07-11).** Audited consolidated FY2025 LK ("Report Final PT Bank Pan Indonesia 31 Desember 2025", panin.co.id, released 2026-02-25, auditor KAP Liana Ramon Xenia & Rekan — member of Deloitte Southeast Asia Limited — unqualified/"tanpa modifikasian" opinion); Q1 2026 unaudited LK ("Buku Lap Keu 31 Mar 26", panin.co.id); secondary press citing these filings verbatim (Bisnis.com, Kontan, PintarSaham, EmitenNews, Databoks) used only where the primary PDF itself returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch — every number below is filing-sourced, none is sell-side. **Access limitation, stated plainly:** panin.co.id and idx.co.id PDF/company-profile fetches were blocked (403) on repeated attempts; I could not open the full audited LK footnotes directly, so the NPL/restructured-loan and related-party-loan footnote depth below is thinner than a full LK read would give — flagged inline wherever it bites, not papered over.

**Profitability & margin path.** ROE (annualized) fell from 5.42% (FY2023) to 4.88% (FY2025); NIM fell from 4.93% (FY2023) to 4.32% (FY2025), with a Q1 2026 estimate near 4.47% (secondary-source estimate, not a disclosed line item — treated as indicative only). This is a bank running well below a reasonable IDR cost of equity, not a high-ROE franchise — the starting point for this thesis is a *mediocre* bank, not a *quality* one. BOPO (opex/income) was 70.22% FY2025, a big improvement from a spiked 79.86% at H1 2024 (H1'24 opex +27.9% yoy to Rp2.75tn) — cost discipline is intact once the one-off H1'24 opex spike rolled off.

**Credit quality — the optics-vs-cash divergence that matters most.** NPL gross has improved every year: 3.53% (2022) → 3.09% (2023) → 3.05% (2024) → 2.82% (FY2025) → 3.00% (Q1 2026). But NPL *net* has risen: 0.90% (2024) → 1.04% (FY2025) — coverage is thinning even as the gross ratio looks better. More decisive: provisioning (impairment/CKPN) expense is rising sharply in cash terms — Rp0.90tn (9M2024) → Rp1.22tn (9M2025), +35.1% yoy (bank's own 9M2025 disclosure, cited via EmitenNews); Rp263.4bn (Q1 2025) → Rp350.7bn (Q1 2026), +33.2% yoy. Per EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS card guidance to trust the provisioning-vs-write-off trend over the accruals-style headline ratio for a bank: the cash provisioning trend is the more decision-relevant signal, and it says credit cost is rising, not falling, even while the gross NPL print improves — consistent with write-offs/restructuring keeping the gross ratio optically clean while real credit cost climbs. I could not obtain restructured-loan / Stage-2 / "dalam perhatian khusus" footnote balances (blocked PDF access) — this is a genuine blind spot, not assumed away. Through-cycle credit cost assumption used below: 110-130bps (above what the improving gross-NPL ratio alone would suggest), roughly Rp1.4-1.6tn/yr annualized on an average ~Rp130tn loan book.

**Funding — the live macro transmission channel.** Q1 2026: CASA Rp60.37tn vs total DPK Rp134.42tn = ~44.9% CASA ratio (55.1% time-deposit funded). DPK fell 6.2% qoq, driven almost entirely by TD run-off (Rp81.95tn→Rp74.05tn, -9.6%) while CASA held far better (-1.6%). Loan book has been shrinking for several consecutive quarters — Rp141.99tn (Q3 2025, -4.72% yoy) → Rp125.17tn (Q1 2026, -3.8% qoq) — with management's own stated reason (Q3 2025 disclosure) being weak "wait and see" credit demand and elevated lending rates, not a capital constraint. LDR ~98% despite the shrinking loan book, because deposits (mainly TD) are shrinking faster — read as the bank deliberately shedding expensive wholesale/TD funding rather than defending balance-sheet size into a rate-hiking cycle. PNBN is NOT a wholesale/JV-funded bank in the multifinance sense (deposits are the funding base, standard VAL_BANKS engine applies) — but its CASA franchise (~45%) is materially weaker than the mega-cap IDX banks, so per the method card's "small-CASA banks squeezed first in tightening" warning, and per Ferrand's macro regime call that BI is defensively hiking (100bp cumulative to 5.75%, chatter of 6% by year-end) directly into bank NIM — funding-cost pressure is a live, not hypothetical, headwind here, and I am NOT assuming NIM re-inflation within the thesis horizon. Sustainable NIM used below: 4.25% (below the FY2025 4.32% print — shaded down, not up, per house instruction to shade conservatively).

**Sustainable ROE build (fundamentals only, no price/valuation used).**
- NIM: 4.25% (through-cycle, shaded below current print given funding-cost headwind, see above)
- Leverage: Assets/Equity = Rp237.32tn / Rp58.77tn = 4.04x (FY2025 actual); not expected to expand — CAR is abundant (37.07% KPMM, Q1 2026, up from 32.4% FY2023 / 30.07% FY2022) and management is shrinking, not growing, the balance sheet
- Credit cost: 110-130bps through-cycle (see above; weighted toward the cash provisioning trend, not the improving headline NPL ratio)
- Opex: BOPO ~70% (normalized FY2025 level)
- DuPont cross-check: implied ROA ~1.05-1.15% × leverage 4.04x ≈ ROE 4.2-4.65%, consistent with (slightly below) the actual FY2025 print of 4.88% — the fundamentals argue for a **roughly flat-to-stable ROE going forward, not an expansion**. This is a load-bearing conclusion: it argues against "quality_bank_rerating" (which needs a high-ROE, durability/expansion story) and toward "washout_rebound" (price mean-reversion despite broadly unchanged, not improving, fundamentals) — see archetype selection below.

**Growth / capital constraint.** Dividend: Rp1.01tn paid ~Jul 2025 (FY2024 earnings); Rp1.0tn / Rp42-per-share declared Jun 2026 (FY2025 earnings) — payout ≈ 35-36% of net income (~Rp2.75-2.87tn). g ≤ ROE×(1-payout) ≈ 4.9% × 0.64 ≈ 3.1%/yr. CET1/CAR headroom is not the binding constraint (37.07% KPMM vs a regulatory minimum roughly 12-13% incl. buffers for this bank's KBMI tier — I could not source a CET1-only breakout separate from total CAR, flagged as a minor data gap, but the headroom is large under either measure; PNBN also carries a Rp3.91tn subordinated bond issued Sep 2024 at 7.25%, likely Tier 2, meaning CET1-only is somewhat below the 37.07% headline but still very high). The realized constraint on growth is **credit demand**, not capital — loan book is currently shrinking (-3.8% to -4.7% recent quarters).

**3y BVPS path (bottom-up, no market price used).** FY2025 equity Rp58.77tn / ~25.615bn shares outstanding (per Q1 2026 EPS back-solve: Rp743.31bn ÷ Rp29.02 EPS) = BVPS₀ ≈ Rp2,294. Compounding retained earnings at g≈3.1%/yr (sustainable ROE 4.9% × 64% retention): BVPS₁≈Rp2,365, BVPS₂≈Rp2,438, BVPS₃≈Rp2,513. Note per EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS: Bank Panin's accounting policy revalues premises/fixed assets to fair value under PSAK 16 (basis-of-preparation note: "historical cost basis except for revaluation of premises..."; historical filings show recurring "transfer of revaluation surplus to retained earnings on disposal of revalued assets") — reported equity/BVPS is inflated versus a pure historical-cost basis by an amount I could not quantify (PDF blocked). Treated as an EARNINGS_QUALITY **optics-class flag**: haircut BVPS-based valuation work qualitatively, noted again in the pre-mortem — this does NOT rise to the card's manipulation-class auto-kill bar (no special notation, no auditor down-tier, unqualified Deloitte-network opinion).

**EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS output contract.**
- Provisioning/write-off trend (3y proxy, cash impairment expense): rising — 9M2024 Rp0.90tn → 9M2025 Rp1.22tn (+35.1%); Q1 2025 Rp263.4bn → Q1 2026 Rp350.7bn (+33.2%) — while NPL gross improves. Diagnosed as a genuine credit-cost uptick, not (or not only) accrual softness.
- IDX board/notation status: no special notation / Papan Pemantauan Khusus flag found for PNBN — checked specifically, none found.
- Related-party % of loan book: **data gap.** Best sourced data point is historical — PNBN consolidated Q4 2020 LK showed related-party loans Rp926,684mn vs third-party Rp120,706,825mn ≈ 0.76% of gross loans. I could NOT access the FY2025/Q1 2026 footnote (panin.co.id PDFs 403'd on every attempt) to confirm whether this still holds — given the family-control structure (see ownership below) this is flagged explicitly as an unresolved blind spot, not assumed to still be ~0.76% today.
- Structure flags: PSAK 16 premises revaluation inflating book value (confirmed, see above — optics-class, haircut applied). No pledged-controlling-stake disclosure, no serial rights issue, no auditor down-tier found in searches conducted — logged as "none found — checked," not omitted.
- Action rule outcome: no manipulation-class flag confirmed → no auto-kill. Two optics-class items (PSAK16 revaluation; related-party data gap) → haircut applied to BVPS-based work + carried into pre-mortem.

**Ownership structure (current, from primary/press-on-primary sources).** Controlling shareholders: ANZ (via Votraint No. 1103 Pty Ltd) 38.82%; founder Mu'min Ali Gunawan (via PT Panin Financial Tbk) 46.04% (as of Sept 2025 shareholder registry, reported via multiple outlets citing IDX disclosure) — implied free float ≈ 15.1%. This is the legacy ANZ joint-control structure (ANZ built to >38% starting ~1999-2009; ANZ + Gunawan formally named joint controllers by OJK in Nov 2019) referenced in the assignment brief — it is still live and unresolved, not historical. As of Dec 2025, press (Kontan, Bisnis.com, Stockbit Snips) reported ANZ may be near a deal to sell its full 38.82% stake to Mu'min Ali Gunawan at a rumored ~0.72x P/BV, with further speculation that Mizuho Financial Group could subsequently consolidate up to ~84.86% of the bank. **This is unconfirmed** — Bank Panin management's own BEI disclosure (2 Dec 2025) states they "cannot speak much, this is a shareholder-level matter," and no signed transaction or OJK/IDX-confirmed deal has been found. Treated as a live ownership overhang / optionality, NOT a dated catalyst (no catalyst_date set) — will be engaged again in variant perception with appropriate hedging.

sections.heading: Bottom-up estimates
sections.detail: Valuation & IDX microstructure (Phase 2 — market data, read only after Bottom-up estimates committed above)
sections.markdown:
**Screen context (2026-07-11, market-data snapshot):** last_price Rp880; off_52w_high_pct -25.96% (implies a 52w high ≈ Rp1,189); mom12_pct -17.07%, mom6_pct -13.85%, mom1_pct +0.75% (a small 1-month bounce inside the broader downtrend); cagr_ann_pct -14.35%; vol_pct 38.18%; 30d ADV Rp3,995,673,916 (~Rp4.0bn/day) — thin, matches the screen's "coverage=thin" tag.

**COE.** 10y FR (IDR) yield 7.26% (TradingEconomics, asof 2026-07-08 — elevated and rising into the BoP-pressure regime Ferrand flagged: persistent capital outflows, IDR weakness, foreign local-bond ownership near a two-decade low) + ERP 5.0% (low end of the house 5.0-6.0% band, argued: 50+ year operating history, Deloitte-network unqualified audit opinion, CAR 37.07%, no manipulation-class governance flag — company-specific funding/franchise risk is already carried in the ROE build below, not a tail-solvency add-on) = **COE ≈ 12.3%**.

**Warranted vs traded P/BV.** Warranted P/BV = (sustainable ROE − g)/(COE − g). Two honest scenarios: (a) current depressed run-rate ROE 4.9%, g 3.0% → (4.9−3.0)/(12.3−3.0) ≈ **0.20x**; (b) a "cycle-normalized" ROE of 5.5% (anchored to the FY2023 5.42% recent high, arguing the NIM/credit-cost squeeze is cyclical, not permanent — Bottom-up), g 3.0% → (5.5−3.0)/(12.3−3.0) ≈ **0.27x**. Traded P/BV at Rp880 vs BVPS₀ Rp2,294 = **0.38x** — ABOVE both warranted estimates. **Stated plainly: the VAL_BANKS residual-income engine does not certify PNBN as statistically cheap versus its own cost of equity right now** — at a 4.9-5.5% sustainable ROE against a 12.3% COE (itself inflated by the current BoP-stress FR curve), a sub-0.3x warranted multiple is the mechanically correct output, and PNBN already trades above that. The PSAK16 premises-revaluation flag (Bottom-up) means true tangible-book P/BV is even higher than 0.38x, tightening this conclusion further, not loosening it. This caps how the edge can honestly be argued below — it is a mean-reversion/overreaction case, not a "hidden compounder trading below DCF fair value" case.

**IDX microstructure.** Free float ≈ 15.1% (100% − ANZ 38.82% − Gunawan/PT Panin Financial 46.04%, Sept 2025 registry). 30d ADV ~Rp4.0bn/day is genuinely thin — a full institutional clip could take several sessions to exit. IDX auto-rejection bands for a Rp200-5,000 stock run ~±25%/session under current exchange rules; on thin ADV, a bad print can gap through a full ARB-Bawah band before a seller is filled — this is exactly what is priced into the kill_criteria/down_pct above (fundamental trigger ~Rp710, ARB-gap-adjusted fill ~Rp530), the mandated gap scenario carried into the pre-mortem below.

**Controlling-family behavior.** The Gunawan family has historically been an entrenching, not distributing, controlling holder — press reporting (Bisnis.com 2019/2024) notes the family was "reluctant to give a board seat" to ANZ despite ANZ's >38% stake, stalling ANZ's own earlier exit attempts for years. Dec 2025 press chatter (Kontan, Stockbit Snips) that ANZ may now be near selling its full stake to Mu'min Ali Gunawan at a rumored ~0.72x P/BV (≈Rp1,652/share — nearly double both the current traded multiple and my own warranted range) is **UNCONFIRMED**: no signed transaction, and Bank Panin management's own 2 Dec 2025 BEI disclosure states they "cannot speak much, this is a shareholder-level matter." I give this very little direct numerical weight (a small blend in the target only, not in p_up/down_pct), but it is a real, primary-sourced data point that the best-informed shareholder in the stock does not price it as a melting ice cube — inconsistent with a pure value-trap read, and I am treating it as upside optionality, not thesis foundation.

**Flows — explicit blind spot.** PNBN carries an em_flows factor tag (screen row), meaning foreign positioning would normally be a live input here. The foreign-flow feed has 0 fresh readings fund-wide (fund-wide stale-data condition) — I am NOT citing any foreign-flow number (live or historical-secondary) as a signal in either direction. This is a real, acknowledged gap in the picture, not a guess.

**Currency.** PNBN is a pure IDR domestic bank (no material FX book disclosed beyond ordinary trade-finance/treasury lines); all levels above and below are in IDR, no FX translation risk to model.

sections.heading: Variant perception
sections.markdown:
**Market believes:** PNBN is a structurally low-ROE, thinly-traded, family-controlled bank in a multi-year downtrend (mom12 -17.07%, cagr -14.35%/yr) that deserves its sub-0.4x P/BV, and that the unresolved ANZ/Gunawan ownership overhang plus a rising 9M2025 provisioning line (+35.1% yoy) are reasons to avoid it until the picture clears — exactly the kind of name thin sell-side coverage lets sit unrepriced in either direction.
**Why wrong:** The magnitude of the price move (-25.96% off the 52w high) is running well ahead of the magnitude of the fundamental move over the comparable window — NIM fell 61bp (4.93%→4.32%, FY2023→FY2025) and ROE fell 54bp (5.42%→4.88%), while the bank stayed solidly profitable, kept a ~35-36% dividend payout intact, improved NPL gross every year (3.53%→2.82%), improved BOPO back to 70.22% after a one-off H1'24 opex spike, and sits on a 37.07% CAR with no notation/manipulation-class governance flag found. Thin coverage means no one is marking this to a normalized-cycle model — the tape is extrapolating the trailing quarter's rising provisioning line without weighing it against the (also real) capital fortress and maintained payout. **Important honesty check:** my own VAL_BANKS math does NOT call PNBN cheap vs COE (warranted P/BV 0.20-0.27x < 0.38x traded) — the mispricing claim here is about the SPEED/SIZE of the drawdown relative to the fundamental change, not a claim that the stock is a hidden compounder trading below intrinsic value.
**What proves us wrong:** NPL net keeps climbing while NPL gross keeps "improving" (confirms write-offs are masking real quality loss rather than genuine coverage discipline — I could not verify the restructured/Stage-2 loan footnote, this is the live blind spot that would resolve it); CASA ratio keeps falling below ~43% as TD costs keep biting (confirms the funding-cost squeeze is structural, not cyclical); the ANZ stake transaction confirms on terms that entrench the family further with zero minority benefit, or collapses acrimoniously, re-widening the overhang discount; or the 10y FR yield keeps climbing past 7.26%, pushing COE higher and the warranted P/BV band lower still.

sections.heading: Disconfirming facts
sections.detail: >=3, observable, current, each citing a dossier/filing line
sections.markdown:
1. NPL net rose from 0.90% (FY2024) to 1.04% (FY2025) even as NPL gross "improved" from 3.05% to 2.82% over the same year — coverage is thinning, not strengthening (FY2025 audited LK, released 2026-02-25, via press citing the release directly).
2. Loan book has contracted for multiple consecutive quarters — Rp141.99tn (Q3 2025, -4.72% yoy) to Rp125.17tn (Q1 2026, -3.8% qoq) — with management's own stated reason being weak "wait and see" credit demand and elevated lending rates, not a capital constraint (Q3 2025 company disclosure via EmitenNews; Q1 2026 LK via PintarSaham).
3. Provisioning/impairment expense is rising sharply in cash terms even as the headline NPL ratio improves — Rp1.22tn (9M2025) vs Rp0.90tn (9M2024), +35.1% yoy; Rp350.7bn (Q1 2026) vs Rp263.4bn (Q1 2025), +33.2% yoy — the exact provisioning-vs-headline-ratio tension the EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS card instructs a bank analyst to weight over the accruals-style ratio (9M2025 disclosure via EmitenNews; Q1 2026 LK via PintarSaham).
4. CASA ratio is ~44.9% (Rp60.37tn of Rp134.42tn DPK, Q1 2026) with 55.1% of funding in time deposits — a structurally weak funding franchise heading into a BI hiking cycle already at 5.75% with chatter of 6% by year-end (Q1 2026 LK via PintarSaham; the macro regime memo, Ferrand, 2026-07-11).

sections.heading: Pre-mortem
sections.markdown: It is late 2027 (1.5y horizon end) and this position lost roughly 30-40%. The most likely reason is: the ARB-gap kill scenario played out exactly as sized — a credit-cost shock (the restructured/Stage-2 loan exposure I could not verify pre-trade, flagged explicitly as a data gap, turned out to be large, and the write-offs that had been flattering the gross-NPL ratio stopped keeping pace with real deterioration) forced a fast repricing; on ~Rp4bn/day ADV, PNBN gapped through its ~25% auto-rejection band and the kill order filled well below the Rp710 trigger, closer to the Rp530 ARB-adjusted level, exactly the mechanism modeled into down_pct. A second, related path: BI's hiking cycle extended past the chattered 6% terminal rate (the BoP-pressure regime never resolved), PNBN's weak ~45% CASA franchise could not defend the margin, NIM broke and stayed below 4.0% for multiple quarters, and the "cyclical squeeze reverses" assumption behind the 5.5% normalized-ROE scenario proved wrong — the depressed 4.9% run-rate WAS the new normal, exactly washout_rebound's own stated failure mode: a value trap where the drawdown was correct. A third, compounding path: the ANZ-to-Gunawan stake transaction (if it happens at all) closed on terms that entrenched the family further with no tag-along/tender benefit to minority holders, removing the one asymmetric-optionality argument in the target, while the related-party lending question I could not resolve (data gap, Bottom-up estimates — no access to the FY2025 footnote) turned out to be the real story sitting underneath the rising provisioning line all along.

sections.heading: Bear attack
sections.markdown:
(Drew appends verbatim; survives the Judge verdict — never edited by a later stage)

**BEAR / Drew — 2026-07-11T14:47:31Z. Verdict: KILL_RECOMMENDED.**

I independently verified against primary-filing-sourced press (panin.co.id/idx.co.id 403'd me too — same access wall the analyst hit). To the analyst's credit, the arithmetic is honest and the numbers largely check out. That is exactly why this must die: the honest numbers say don't buy, and the thesis buys anyway.

**0. FACT-CHECK OF LOAD-BEARING NUMBERS (verified, primary-sourced press citing the filings).**
- ROE 4.88% FY2025, NIM 4.32%, NPL gross 2.82% / net 1.04%, equity Rp58.77tn, BVPS ~Rp2,282, EPS Rp114.24: CONFIRMED (PintarSaham FY2025 analysis of the audited LK). Traded P/BV ≈0.39x at Rp880 — analyst's 0.38x is right. No fabrication in the headline set.
- Q1 2026 provisioning Rp350.7bn vs Rp263.4bn (+33.2%), NPL gross 3.00%, CASA Rp60.37tn/DPK Rp134.42tn: CONFIRMED (PintarSaham Q1'26).
- **BUT the central "credit cost is rising" narrative is a 9M cherry-pick.** FY2025 audited CKPN/impairment came in ~Rp1.44tn, DOWN ~14.79% yoy (Bisnis/PintarSaham on the audited release) — the exact opposite of the "+35.1%" 9M framing the analyst built disconfirming-fact #3 and the whole "optics-vs-cash divergence" section on. The Q4'24 base had a provisioning spike that rolled off. The provisioning line is choppy (up 9M'25, down FY'25, up Q1'26), not the monotonic "rising credit cost" story the thesis leans on. Not fabrication, but selective-window framing on a load-bearing narrative element — a Judge should down-weight the analyst's earnings-quality read accordingly.
- **Related-party loans (the flagged stale Q4-2020 0.76% substitute):** I also could not retrieve the FY2025/Q1'26 footnote. RULING: this does NOT trigger the fabricated-load-bearing-input auto-kill, because the analyst did NOT use 0.76% as a positive input — it is transparently flagged as an unresolved gap and given zero weight in p_up/target. Honest handling. HOWEVER it is load-bearing to the DOWNSIDE/governance case and cannot be underwritten: you are buying a family-controlled bank at the precise moment its one arms-length co-controller (ANZ, 38.82%) is trying to exit, which would lift the founder to ~84.86% control — and you cannot see the related-party loan book that sits underneath a rising Q1'26 provisioning line. That is an un-underwritable governance risk that alone should cap sizing near zero.

**1. ESTIMATES AT WIDEST HONEST ERROR BAR.** Warranted P/BV = (ROE−g)/(COE−g). At the analyst's own COE 12.3% (itself generous — the 10y FR at 7.26% is rising, and ERP was pinned at the 5.0% FLOOR of the house band; use mid-band 5.5% → COE 12.8% → warranted P/BV 0.19-0.25x): warranted range 0.19-0.27x. On BVPS ~Rp2,294 that is a warranted price of **Rp436-619**. Spot is Rp880. **The stock trades 42-102% ABOVE the house engine's fair value.** The PSAK16 premises-revaluation flag (analyst's own) and the presence of minority interest in the Rp58.77tn total-equity BVPS (parent-only book is lower) both push true tangible attributable P/BV HIGHER than 0.39x — tightening the overvaluation, never loosening it. There is no honest fundamental error bar in which this stock is cheap.

**2. THE VARIANT PERCEPTION IS INCOHERENT.** "The market will notice the drawdown overshot the fundamental deterioration" cannot coexist with "my own engine says the stock is 40-100% overvalued on those same fundamentals." If the market fully re-rates PNBN to what the fundamentals warrant, the stock goes to Rp436-619 — i.e., DOWN 30-50% from here, not up. The variant reduces to: "the tape overshot on the way down, so it should bounce on the way back up regardless of fair value." That is textbook mean-reversion chart-reading wearing a residual-income costume. The VAL_BANKS engine was run, produced a sell signal, and was then explicitly set aside for a "capped technical/blend" target. Strip the bank analysis and the thesis is: it fell 26%, small names overshoot, buy the bounce.

**3. TARGET IS UNMOORED FROM ANYTHING FUNDAMENTAL.** Target Rp1,270 is (a) ABOVE the implied 52-week high of ~Rp1,189 — this is not a "partial retracement," it is a fresh high — and (b) 2.1-2.9x the engine's warranted fair value. Back-solving the exit_plan blend (1,270 = w·1,652 + (1−w)·1,189) gives **w ≈ 0.175 weight on the unconfirmed ANZ→Gunawan 0.72x rumor** — that is not "very little weight," it is ~18% of the upper anchor riding on an M&A rumor, on a thesis with catalyst_date: null.

**4. WRONG ARCHETYPE — BOTH PILLARS OF washout_rebound FAIL.** The prior (0.45, n=60) requires "quality intact + forced selling," and its stated dominant failure is "a value trap where the drawdown was correct (governance, structural demand loss)." (i) Quality is NOT intact: ROE 4.88% against COE 12.3% means the bank earns ~40% of its cost of equity — it is DESTROYING economic value every year while nominally profitable. That is impaired earnings power, the definition of a value trap, not a "fundamentally intact" name. (ii) "Forced selling / foreign-flow capitulation" is UNVERIFIABLE — the flow feed is stale fund-wide and the analyst cites no z-score. Both required edge conditions are absent; PNBN also carries the structural-demand-loss red flag (loan book shrinking multiple quarters on "wait-and-see" demand) and the governance red flag. The analyst shaded p_up only 3pp (0.45→0.42) — a token haircut where the honest analog sits in value-trap territory (~0.30-0.33).

**5. SIZING / EV MATH — THE POSITIVE EV IS AN ILLUSION AND IT LOSES TO A BOND.** ev_math price component = 0.42·44 + 0.58·(−40) = **−4.72%**. The ONLY reason expected_pct prints +1.13% is ~6.4% of dividends over 1.5y. So the price bet is negative-EV and the trade "works" solely on a dividend — a dividend that (see §6) is being paid against NEGATIVE operating cash flow out of non-core trading gains. Now the decisive test, using the fund's OWN capital hurdle (the base-rate library fr_duration_carry: "equities deserve capital only when the expected equity premium over the FR curve exceeds ~4%/yr"): expected return 1.13% / 1.5y = **0.75%/yr** vs the 10y FR at **7.26%/yr** → equity risk premium **≈ −6.5%/yr**. The trade must clear +4%/yr; it comes in ~10.5pp BELOW the bar, and NEGATIVE versus simply holding the government bond in the same book. On sizing mechanics: down_pct −40% (kill fill ~Rp530, ARB-gap-adjusted) is internally consistent, but likely still optimistic — warranted fair value Rp436-619 sits at/below the kill level, so a plain re-rating to fair value (no credit shock needed) already delivers −30% to −50%, and a thin-tape gap can overshoot further. On Rp4.0bn/day ADV with 15.1% float, 20%-ADV exit capacity is ~Rp0.8bn/day — any position of institutional size takes many sessions to unwind and the kill order eats the gap; this alone argues sizing near zero.

**6. NEW DISCONFIRMING FACT (not in thesis).** FY2025 net income Rp2.87tn (+0.13%) was propped by NON-CORE gains — commission/fee income +3.47% to Rp2.30tn "mainly from securities transaction profits," plus fair-value marks — while NET INTEREST INCOME was STAGNANT ~Rp8.9tn and lending contracted −2.78%. Critically, **FY2025 operating cash flow was NEGATIVE Rp1.88tn, reversed from +Rp19tn** (CNBC Indonesia, "Alarm Bank Papan Tengah! Panin Mandek," 2026-04-20; EmitenNews on the audited release). The bull thesis's load-bearing "maintained profitability + intact ~35% dividend = capital fortress" pillar is therefore LOW-QUALITY: the profit is trading-gain-flattered and the dividend — the sole source of positive EV in ev_math — is being paid out of a bank whose operating cash flow just went negative. The thesis's own EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS pass examined provisioning and PSAK16 but never inspected income COMPOSITION or cash flow, and missed this entirely.

**7. STEELMAN OF PRE-MORTEM — UNMENTIONED FAILURE MODE.** The pre-mortem covers credit shock, NIM squeeze, and a bad stake deal. It omits the most probable and most boring failure: **the ANZ sale process is already documented as STALLED over a pricing mismatch** — sellers wanted >2x current P/BV (~1.5x book); CIMB and DBS both looked at the whole ~86% and walked without binding bids because they would not pay the family's price (Reuters/Yahoo, 2025-07-04, at Rp1,140). So the market's most sophisticated potential buyers, with full diligence access, declined to pay up for control of this bank. The "optionality" the target leans ~18% on is a deal real buyers rejected. Failure mode: no deal, no bounce, and the stock simply grinds toward warranted fair value while the holder collects a shrinking, cash-flow-uncovered dividend and cannot exit the thin tape without moving the price.

**8. ANTI-GAMING INSPECTION.** Estimates committed 14:32:10Z before draft 14:37:59Z — discipline OK. kill 530 < entry 880 < target 1270 holds; ev_math up/down_pct tie to the levels arithmetically. No frontmatter tampering. Two soft flags: (a) the "+1.13% expected" headline masks a −4.72% price-EV carried entirely by an at-risk dividend; (b) p_up shaded only 3pp below a base rate whose two qualifying conditions both fail — the deviation runs the wrong direction relative to the evidence.

**9. VERDICT: KILL_RECOMMENDED.** By the fund's own math — a stock trading 42-102% above the house engine's warranted fair value, an expected return of 0.75%/yr that yields a NEGATIVE ~6.5%/yr equity risk premium versus the FR sovereign in the same book, an archetype whose two required edge conditions both fail, and a sole positive-EV component (the dividend) funded out of non-core trading gains against negative operating cash flow — this is a value trap with a technical target painted over a sell signal, and no resizing repairs the fact that you are paying up to catch a bounce the fundamentals do not support.

sections.heading: Revision
sections.markdown:
**Sunda (ANALYST_INDO), 2026-07-12, in response to Drew's 2026-07-11T14:47:31Z KILL_RECOMMENDED attack.**

Read Drew's attack in full before writing this. His case holds up. Every change below is a lowering of an estimate, a cut to p_up/up_pct, a widening of down_pct, or a haircut to the dividend assumption — nothing is being raised. I have no flagged "new evidence" that would license raising anything: the two genuinely new facts Bear introduces (points 6 and 7) both cut against the thesis, not for it. Responding to each numbered point in order:

**0.** Agreed on both counts, with one nuance on the second. The related-party/governance point stands in full: flagging the FY2025/Q1'26 related-party footnote as an unresolved gap and giving it zero weight was honest handling, but Bear is right that a data gap sitting directly under a live co-controller-exit process is not merely "unresolved" — it is un-underwritable. I now treat it as a standalone reason to keep sizing near zero regardless of the point-estimate EV, reflected below in the widened ARB-gap assumption on the kill level. On the "9M cherry-pick": fair criticism of my framing. FY2025 audited CKPN/impairment was actually DOWN ~14.79% yoy on a full-year basis, so "provisioning is rising" is not the monotonic story disconfirming fact #3 implied — it's choppy (up 9M'24→9M'25, down FY2025, up again +33.2% yoy Q1 2026). I should not have built that disconfirming fact and the "optics-vs-cash divergence" framing on the 9M window alone without flagging the full-year reversal. I am not reversing the underlying concern (Q1 2026 is still a fresh acceleration and choppiness itself is not reassuring for a bank this thinly covered), but I concede the original presentation overstated its consistency.

**1.** Accepted, arithmetic conceded. At mid-band ERP (5.5%, not the 5.0% floor I used) COE rises to ~12.8% and warranted P/BV falls to 0.19-0.25x — a warranted price of Rp436-619 against a Rp880 traded price, i.e. 42-102% overvaluation on the house's own engine. I did not have a defensible reason to sit at the floor of the house ERP band for a bank carrying a live governance overhang and a sub-45% CASA franchise heading into a hiking cycle; mid-band is the more honest choice. This flows into the kill-level revision at point 5.

**2.** Agreed — this is the strongest point in the attack and I did not resolve it in the original draft. A thesis cannot simultaneously argue "the market will re-rate this toward the fundamentals" and "my own fundamentals-based engine says fair value is 30-50% below spot." I am resolving the incoherence by relabeling, not papering over: this is now explicitly a technical-overreaction/mean-reversion bet on the SIZE of the drawdown relative to the SIZE of the fundamental move, made in full knowledge that it runs counter to the residual-income fair value — not a claim that the stock is undervalued. A technical-only case is inherently weaker support than a fundamentals-backed one, which is part of why p_up is cut hard at point 4.

**3.** Agreed, and this was an arithmetic error on my part, not just an aggressive judgment call: Rp1,270 is mechanically above the implied 52-week high of Rp1,189, so calling it a "partial retracement" was wrong on the numbers — it was a fresh high dressed up as a retracement. The back-solved ~17.5% weight on the unconfirmed ANZ-to-Gunawan rumor is also higher than I represented it as ("very little weight") when I wrote the original exit_plan. I am removing the rumor weighting from the target entirely (see point 7 for why "trim" isn't enough) and replacing it with a plain retracement: 880 + 0.55x(1,189-880) ~= **Rp1,050**. Frontmatter updated: target 1,270 -> 1,050; up_pct 44 -> 19 (matches (1050/880-1)x100 = 19.3%, within lint tolerance). This is a genuine partial retracement, below the 52w high, with no M&A optionality baked in.

**4.** Agreed. Sustainable ROE 4.88-4.9% against COE 12.3-12.8% is value destruction, not "quality intact" — that pillar fails outright, it isn't a close call. "Forced selling" is unverifiable with a stale fund-wide flow feed and no z-score cited; I should have flagged that I could not evidence this pillar rather than selecting the archetype as if I had. Both required qualifying conditions of washout_rebound fail, and the archetype's own notes name the exact failure mode PNBN fits: "a value trap where the drawdown was correct." There is no `value_trap` key in the base-rate library to remap `archetype:` to, so that field stays `washout_rebound` — but I am no longer treating the 0.45 library rate as a light-haircut anchor. p_up cut to **0.30**, which is exactly the calibration-clamp floor the house rules permit pre-n_own>=10 (|posterior-prior|0.42) ran in the wrong direction relative to the evidence; this corrects it.

**5.** Agreed on the mechanics, and the corrected numbers are worse than the attack itself computed. Price-EV at the new p_up/up_pct/down_pct: 0.30x19 + 0.70x(-48) = 5.7 - 33.6 = **-27.9%**, more negative than Bear's original -4.72% because the target came down proportionally more than the kill level moved. On the kill level: Bear is right that my original Rp530 fill assumed only a single 25% ARB band, and that the warranted-value floor (Rp436-619) sits at/inside that level — meaning a plain re-rate needs no fresh credit-deterioration signal to get there. Given the governance flag now established (point 0) plus the pre-existing thin-ADV/low-float profile, the SIZING_EV_BASE_RATES card's own instruction is to assume the worse end of its 15-35% ARB-gap range for a name like this. Widened to a 35% single-band haircut: 710x0.65 ~= **Rp460** (kill_criteria updated; was Rp530), giving down_pct **-48%** (was -40%). Also cutting net_div_yield_pct_pa 4.3% -> **2.8%** (point 6). New expected_pct = 0.30x19 + 0.70x(-48) + 2.8x1.5 - 0.6 = **-24.3%** (was +1.13%). Annualized over the 1.5y washout_rebound horizon that is ~-16.2%/yr against the 10y FR at 7.26%/yr — an equity risk premium of roughly **-23.5%/yr**, materially worse than Bear's already-damning -6.5%/yr, and nowhere near the fund's own +4%/yr equity-vs-FR hurdle. I agree sizing should sit at or near zero; that decision is formally PM's/Risk's, but I am not recommending a live position at these numbers.

**6.** Accepted as a genuine new disconfirming fact I missed. My EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS pass checked the provisioning trend, the NPL gross/net divergence, and PSAK16 — it never checked income composition or the cash flow statement, which was a real gap in my own process, not a judgment call. FY2025 operating cash flow swinging to -Rp1.88tn from +Rp19tn, with net income instead propped by securities-trading gains while NII stagnated and lending contracted -2.78%, directly undermines the "maintained ~35% payout = capital fortress" framing I used in Bottom-up and in Variant Perception. The dividend is the ONLY positive-EV component in this thesis and I can no longer treat it as fully cash-generation-backed. Haircutting net_div_yield_pct_pa 4.3% -> **2.8%** (~35% cut) to price in payout-cut risk over the horizon — consistent with the dividend_income_anchor archetype's own dominant-failure note ("the yield must be defended by cash generation, not by a falling price"), applicable here by analogy even though washout_rebound remains the primary archetype key.

**7.** Agreed, and this changes how the M&A optionality should have been treated from the start. I called the ANZ-to-Gunawan rumor "unconfirmed" and said I gave it "very little weight," but point 3 shows the target math actually leaned on it (~17.5%). Bear's new fact — CIMB and DBS both diligenced the ~86% stake and walked without a binding bid at Rp1,140, below even the rumored 0.72x transfer level — is direct evidence that the two best-informed potential buyers in the world declined to pay up for control of this bank. That is a reason to treat the optionality as low-probability-of-attractive-terms, not just "unconfirmed." Removed from the target entirely at point 3 rather than trimmed; carried forward only as an unweighted watch item.

**8.** Agreed on both soft flags. The dividend-masking-a-negative-price-EV structure is now explicit and corrected in point 5's numbers. The 3pp haircut ran the wrong direction relative to the evidence — corrected to the calibration-clamp floor at point 4.

**9.** I concur with the direction of the verdict. After this revision the thesis shows a negative price-EV (-27.9%), a negative expected total return (-24.3% over 1.5y), an equity risk premium versus the FR sovereign of roughly -23.5%/yr, an archetype whose two qualifying conditions both fail with no better-fitting key available in the house library, a target with no remaining fundamental or credible-optionality support, and an un-underwritable governance blind spot opening at the worst possible moment. I cannot change `status`/`verdict` — that is the Judge's call next — but my own honest reading of my own revised numbers agrees with Bear's: this does not clear the bar.

**Process note.** Per the ANALYST_INDO Revision protocol, multiple ev_math fields moved >20% relative to their pre-revision values (p_up -28.6%, up_pct -56.8%, down_pct +20.0% at the threshold, net_div_yield_pct_pa -34.9%, expected_pct sign-flipped from +1.13% to -24.3%). This revision should route back to Drew before the Judge, per that rule, rather than straight to a Judge verdict.

**BEAR RE-ATTACK — Drew — 2026-07-12T16:05:00Z — VERDICT: KILL_RECOMMENDED**

Re-attack scope only: I fact-checked this thesis's load-bearing numbers exhaustively in my 2026-07-11T14:47:31Z pass and am not repeating that work. This pass verifies the Revision itself: did it honestly answer every point, do the new numbers actually foot, and did the revision process introduce any new tell.

**1. Completeness — every numbered point answered, none dodged.** Sunda's Revision addresses points 0 through 9 in order, matching my numbering exactly. No point is skipped, relabeled to dodge, or answered with a non-responsive concession. Point 9 correctly declines to touch `status`/`verdict` (Judge's job) while stating agreement with my math — that's the right boundary, not a dodge.

**2. Arithmetic re-derived independently — it foots, and it foots against the analyst, not for them.**
- Price-EV: 0.30×19 + 0.70×(−48) = 5.7 − 33.6 = **−27.9%**. Matches.
- Dividend leg: 2.8%/yr × 1.5y horizon = 4.2%. Total: −27.9 + 4.2 − 0.6(drag) = **−24.3%**. Matches `ev_math.expected_pct` in frontmatter exactly.
- up_pct: (1050/880−1)×100 = 19.32% → booked as 19 (0.32pp off, inside the ±3pp lint band). down_pct: (460/880−1)×100 = −47.73% → booked as −48 (0.27pp off, inside band). Both clean.
- Kill level: fundamental trigger 710 × (1−0.35 ARB haircut) = 461.5 → rounded to 460. Rounds down, not up — the direction that (trivially, ~0.3%) favors the position, not against it. Immaterial but noting it because I said I'd check every direction.
- Annualized: −24.3%/1.5y = −16.2%/yr; ERP vs the 10y FR at 7.26% = **−23.46%/yr**, matches the stated "roughly −23.5%/yr." Worse than my original −6.5%/yr by a full order of magnitude in the wrong direction for the bull.
- Calibration clamp citation verified verbatim against `the base-rate library` line 36: `"clamp |posterior-prior| =10"`. 0.45 − 0.15 = 0.30 exactly. No `value_trap` key exists in the file (confirmed by direct search) — the archetype-key claim is honest, not a convenient dodge.
- ARB-gap citation verified against `agents/methods/SIZING_EV_BASE_RATES.md` §5: "assume kill exits fill 1–2 ARB bands (15–35%)... for high-retail-float or governance-flagged names." 35% is the card's own stated ceiling, correctly maxed out for a name that is now both thin-float AND governance-flagged — not an invented number.

I could not find a single field where the correction moved the wrong way. This is the cleanest revision arithmetic I've reviewed at this desk.

**3. Where it still, if anything, UNDERSTATES the damage — three places.**
(a) p_up=0.30 is presented, honestly, as a *rule-imposed floor* ("the most honest deviation the house rules permit"), not the analyst's true posterior. Both qualifying conditions of `washout_rebound` fail and PNBN sits in the archetype's own named dominant-failure bucket verbatim ("a value trap where the drawdown was correct"). An unconstrained estimate here would plausibly sit below 0.30 — the calibration clamp is doing the flattering, not the analyst, and it's disclosed rather than hidden, but the Judge should read −24.3%/−23.5%/yr ERP as a FLOOR on how bad this looks, not a center estimate.
(b) net_div_yield_pct_pa cut to 2.8% (from 4.3%, a 35% haircut) still assumes roughly two-thirds of the prior yield survives, against a bank whose FY2025 operating cash flow just went NEGATIVE Rp1.88tn (from +Rp19tn) and whose controlling family has a documented history of entrenching rather than distributing (my point 7). A dividend paid out of trading gains and book reserves rather than operating cash, held by a family under no minority pressure, is a full-suspension risk, not just a trim risk — 2.8% may still be generous.
(c) The surviving 30% up-case still assumes a clean, no-fundamental-support technical retracement to Rp1,050 fires cleanly. But the archetype's own failure mode for exactly this setup is typically "no bounce at all, just further grind" — the up leg itself, even shrunk to p=0.30, may still be too clean an outcome to assign that much probability mass to.

None of these are corrections I'm forcing back into the numbers — the calibration-clamp and SIZING_EV_BASE_RATES ceiling are both legitimate house rules, and the analyst used them correctly and transparently. I flag them only to answer the "does the revision now overcorrect/underclaim" question the re-attack protocol requires: the answer is it undercorrects if anything, never overcorrects.

**4. Anti-gaming inspection of the revision itself.** No new anomaly. Every moved field ran in the bear-favoring direction (p_up down, up_pct down, down_pct more negative, kill level lower, target lower, dividend yield down, expected_pct sign-flipped negative) — nothing was quietly raised without a flagged `new evidence:` citation, satisfying the fund record revision rule. The missing `{stage: revised, actor: ANALYST_INDO, at: ...}` stage_log stamp is real, but I checked: T-GLOBAL-NVO-001 and T-GLOBAL-TXN-001 both carry the identical gap on their own Revision sections, and the thesis linter's stage_log check enforces ordering, not a revision stamp — this is a norm-without-a-ruler across the whole pipeline (fund record meta-principle 1), already flagged by other Bear passes, not a tell specific to this analyst gaming this file. No cherry-picked framing, no performative concessions — every "agreed" is followed by re-derived arithmetic, not just an apology. This reads as a genuinely rigorous self-correction.

**5. Verdict: KILL_RECOMMENDED, unchanged and, if anything, reinforced.** The Revision didn't just fail to save the trade — it independently re-derived a materially worse number than my own original attack (−23.5%/yr ERP vs. my −6.5%/yr), using arithmetic I verified line-by-line and could not fault in either direction, and every remaining soft spot in its assumptions (the p_up floor, the dividend haircut, the up-case cleanliness) still leans generous to the bull, not against it. There is no honest path left in this file to a positive expected return; the strongest sentence against the trade is now the analyst's own: this stock offers a −23.5%/yr equity risk premium against the fund's own sovereign-bond alternative in the same book, and the single number keeping the headline from looking even worse — the dividend — is being paid out of a bank whose operating cash flow just turned negative for the first time.

sections.markdown: **KILL — reason_tag=valuation.** Lint passes clean (structure, EV arithmetic ±3pp, archetype registry membership all green — only a word-count warning, non-blocking); the stage_log chain is monotonic and precise (estimates_committed 14:32:10Z 0.30, up_pct 44->19, down_pct -40->-48, net_div_yield 4.3->2.8, expected_pct +1.13->-24.3) — so the revision process itself is clean; the thesis simply has no honest path left to a positive expected return, on a name that is also thin-float (15.1%) and governance-flagged (live co-controller-exit process atop an unresolved related-party-loan blind spot) at the moment sizing would matter most.
